what_works: Geopolitical & National Relevance: Videos focused on India's standing, military, economy, and borders generate the highest views (India's Highest-Earning Cities: 3,516 views; Top 5 Powerful Countries/India: 3,316 views; 1962 War: 2,617 views; Maritime Boundary: 2,313 views).

Curiosity Loops & Confrontational Titles: Titles asking direct questions or pitting two entities against each other ('भारत किस नंबर पर है?', 'US vs North Korea', 'क्या UK टूटने वाला है?') consistently surpass the 1,248 median.
Morning Upload Window: 4 out of the top 4 videos were published between 6:00 AM and 9:00 AM IST.
Hinglish / Hindi Title Blends: Combining Hindi script or Hinglish curiosity hooks with clear visual emojis outperforms sterile English titles.

diagnosis.hook: Underperforming videos give away the answer in the title/first 2 seconds (e.g., 'Romans' Concrete HEALS ITSELF') or sound like middle-school science lectures ('Photosynthesis Explained'). Winning videos frame a comparative puzzle or national question within the first frame.
diagnosis.buildup: Low performers suffer from flat informational recitation without progression or rising stakes. Because retention data is unavailable, this is reflected in stagnant views despite high like ratios (people who stay like it, but the algorithm drops distribution due to immediate swipe-aways).
diagnosis.visuals: Recent low-view videos (sub-100) completely abandoned custom thumbnails and emoji visual framing. Educational facts need immediate high-contrast maps, split screens, or zoom-ins rather than static b-roll or stock footage.
diagnosis.titles_topics: Major topic drift: The channel drifted from high-performing geopolitics, military defense, and Indian superlatives into random biology (shrimp, axolotl, plants) and obscure foreign history. The audience did not subscribe for school science.
diagnosis.other: Metadata negligence in weak videos (leaving 'Description:' in titles, zero tags, empty descriptions) coupled with shifting away from the proven 6-9 AM IST publishing window.

hook_rules: Never reveal the core answer or payoff in the title or the first 3 seconds.
Start the voiceover with a high-stakes open loop: 'Do you know why...', 'This single mistake cost...', or 'What if I told you...'.
Display on-screen text in bold Hindi/English contrasting yellow-and-white in the upper third within frame 1.
Incorporate immediate movement or sound FX (whoosh, hit, record scratch) at 0:00 to arrest feed scrolling.
For comparison videos, state the rivalries immediately (e.g., 'Country A thought it was impossible, but Country B did this...').
buildup_rules: Use the '3-Layer Fact Structure': Layer 1 (Common belief), Layer 2 (The hidden twist), Layer 3 (The shocking outcome).
Change visual perspective, zoom level, or b-roll every 1.5 to 2.5 seconds to sustain visual pacing.
Hold the #1 rank, final conclusion, or pivotal fact until the final 5 seconds before the loop.
Ensure seamless audio looping where the final sentence connects logically into the opening hook.
visual_rules: Always set an explicit custom frame or uploaded thumbnail featuring high-contrast subjects and an expressive focal point.
Use map animations with glowing borders for all geopolitical, war, and border topics (historically your strongest niche).
Overlay kinetic captions (word-by-word highlight) to retain viewers watching with muted or low audio.
Avoid sterile white-background textbook graphics; use dark-themed, cinematic grade overlays with subtle motion.
title_rules: Blend Hindi curiosity with English keywords (e.g., 'दुनिया का सबसे रहस्यमयी... Mystery of...').
Include exactly 1-2 emotional trigger emojis (🇮🇳, 😱, 🔥, 💀) to catch the eye in notifications and search.
Keep title length under 60 characters so it does not get truncated on mobile Shorts UI.
Thoroughly sanitize titles before publishing to prevent metadata accidents like 'Description:' or '#shorts' spam.
topic_rules: Focus exclusively on 3 proven pillars: Indian Superlatives/Economics, Geopolitics & Border Mysteries, and High-Stakes Historical Conflicts.
Validate every topic against the 'So What?' test: If it does not spark national pride, fear, or disbelief, discard it.
Benchmark topics against search interest: Avoid curriculum-based school topics (biology, general botany) unless framed as a bizarre dark mystery.
avoid: Publishing school curriculum or textbook concepts ('Photosynthesis Explained', generic animal facts).
Switching to cold, 100% English academic titles that alienate Hindi/Hinglish speaking viewers.
Spoiling the climax or solution in the title.
Uploading during afternoon dead zones (12 PM - 4 PM IST); stick strictly to the 6 AM - 9 AM IST morning window.
Uploading without tags, relevant descriptions, or thumbnail verification.
